name: Texas Madrone

facts.where: Rocky Hill Country and West Texas slopes

caution: Mealy and only mildly sweet; eaten in moderation. Prized more as a beautiful tree than a heavy food. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Unmistakable smooth peeling bark in cream, pink, and terracotta, with clusters of round red-orange fruit. A slow-growing Hill Country treasure worth protecting.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The grainy berries are pleasant fresh in small amounts and cook into a mild jelly.
